title: A creation walk
hookLine: a weekly walk to notice God's world
tomorrow: why did Paul want the money set aside before he arrived?

lines: BEHOLD THE FOWLS OF THE AIR.
cards: Earbuds in, podcast on, eyes on the sidewalk, and by the time you're home you haven't seen a single thing.
Now a hillside, and a crowd full of the same worries people carry on any sidewalk: what will we eat, what will we wear. Jesus doesn't hand them a plan.
He points up, at birds crossing the sky: “Behold the fowls of the air.” Then he looks down at the wildflowers in the grass, and says something startling about a king.

teach.h: THEY SOW NOT, YET ARE FED.
teach.b: First the birds, in the King James Bible: “Behold the fowls of the air: for they sow not, neither do they reap, nor gather into barns; yet your heavenly Father feedeth them.”

Then the flowers, and the king: “Consider the lilies of the field, how they grow; they toil not, neither do they spin: And yet I say unto you, That even Solomon in all his glory was not arrayed like one of these.”
Solomon in all his glory loses to a wildflower.
Here's what to notice: Jesus answers worry with an assignment for the eyes. Behold. Consider.
How they grow. Not a glance on the way past; looking long enough to see something. The setting matters too.
Just before, he says: “Take no thought for your life, what ye shall eat, or what ye shall drink.” The lilies aren't decoration. They're his argument.
The Psalms read the world the same way, as something that speaks: “The heavens declare the glory of God; and the firmament sheweth his handywork.”
A creation walk takes that seriously, once a week. No headphones, no step count to beat.
Just a slow walk where the sky, a tree, or a weed in a crack gets a full look, and for those who pray, the looking turns into thanks.

how: Some Christians take a regular slow walk outdoors, without music or podcasts, to notice creation and give thanks, sometimes carrying a line from Matthew 6 or a psalm with them.

o: a weekly slow walk to notice God's world
a pilgrimage on foot to a holy place far away
an outdoor service held once a year in summer

his words are behold and consider: look long enough to see how they grow.

games.q: your little brother can't stop asking what-ifs about his new school. you've tried answering every one. what does the hillside teaching try instead?
o: a walk outside to look closely at birds and flowers.
a list of every what-if, each solved one by one.
telling him that worry means he doesn't trust enough.
games.why: Jesus answers worry with an assignment for the eyes: behold the fowls, consider the lilies, how they grow.

practice: Stand and walk for a minute, to a window, a door, or out onto a step, with nothing in your ears. Find one living thing, a tree, a weed, a bird, the sky, and give it a full look: how it grows, what color it really is.
If you pray, let the looking turn into thanks.

wordCard.voice: A creation walk. A weekly slow walk with the headphones out, where looking at what grows becomes a way to set worry down.

carryVoice: The line to take with you: consider the lilies, how they grow, dressed finer than Solomon ever was. See you tomorrow.
